subtitle: Basic op-amp circuits, real limits, and the capstone measurement amplifier
takeaways: Negative feedback: the resistors set the gain
Use an INA for bridges; resistor matching sets CMRR
Keep G < 100 per stage; watch offset and headroom

slides.title: Op-amp and the golden rules
bullets: Amplifies V_{+} − V_{−} with A = 10^{5} … 10^{7}; output stays inside supply
Open loop: ±135 µV linear range, else a rail → comparator
Negative feedback to the inverting input pulls V_{+} − V_{−} to ≈ 0
Rule 1 holds only while the output is not saturated
slides.rule: With negative feedback: V_{+} = V_{−} and I_{+} = I_{−} = 0
slides.notes: The plot shows the open-loop transfer: a few hundred microvolts saturate the output. Golden rules from Horowitz/Hill; the property table ideal vs. real is in section The Ideal Operational Amplifier.

slides.title: Voltage follower: buffer the source
bullets: V_{out} = V_{in}, gain 1; input current ≈ 0, output low impedance
100k/100k divider with 10 kΩ load: 0.833 V instead of 5 V
Behind a follower: 5.00 V, the divider does not notice the load
Used at bridge taps, ADC reference ladder, S&H hold capacitor

falstad.name: opamp_follower
falstad.hint: Compare the loaded divider (0.833 V) with the buffered one (5.00 V)

slides.notes: The follower amplifies current, not voltage: it copies a high-impedance node to a low-impedance output.

slides.title: Non-inverting vs. inverting amplifier

left.head: Non-inverting
bullets: G = 1 + R_{2}/R_{1}, in phase
Input resistance ≈ ∞
Gain ≥ 1 only

right.head: Inverting
bullets: V_{−} is a virtual ground
Input resistance = R_{1} (loads source)

slides.notes: Both follow from the two golden rules in two lines. The figure shows the non-inverting amplifier: R1 and R2 divide the output back to the inverting input.

slides.title: Falstad: G = 3 and G = −2

falstad.name: opamp_noninv_inv
falstad.hint: Scope: ±1.50 V in phase and ±1.00 V inverted for 0.5 V in

observe: Same R_{1} = 10 kΩ, R_{2} = 20 kΩ in both circuits
Non-inverting: 1.5 V, in phase; inverting: 1.0 V, inverted
Try R_{2} = 47 kΩ for an inverting gain of −4.7
slides.notes: Input 0.5 V amplitude at 1 kHz. Exercise 6.1 asks for gains, amplitudes and input resistances.

slides.title: Summing amplifier
bullets: Virtual ground decouples the inputs; currents add up in R_{f}
Weight of input k: −R_{f}/R_{k}
Uses: audio mixer, weighted DAC, adding an offset (level shift)

falstad.name: opamp_summing
falstad.hint: Vout = −1.50 V, summing node stays at 0.00 V

slides.notes: Inputs 1 V via 10 kΩ, 2 V via 20 kΩ and −0.5 V via 10 kΩ with Rf = 10 kΩ. Exercise 6.2.

slides.title: Difference amplifier and CMRR
bullets: CMRR = A_{D}/A_{CM}; set by resistor matching, not the op-amp
G = 10, R_{4} 1 % high: 72.6 mV instead of 50.0 mV (+45 %)
Remedy: 0.1 % or matched networks, trimmer, integrated diff. amp
slides.rule: Worst case: CMRR ≈ (1 + G)/(4ε), 1 % parts, G = 10: ≈ 275 (49 dB)

falstad.name: opamp_diffamp
falstad.hint: Matched 50.0 mV vs. 1 % mismatch 72.6 mV at 2.5 V common mode

slides.notes: A symmetric bridge has 2.5 V common mode and some 10 mV signal, so a tiny common-mode gain is a big error. The input resistances are unequal and low: the circuit loads a bridge. Exercise 6.3.

slides.title: Instrumentation amplifier (INA)
bullets: A1, A2 non-inverting: inputs draw no current, bridge not loaded
Input stage: differential gain 1 + 2R/R_{G}, common mode gain 1
A3 difference stage removes the common mode
One R_{G} sets the gain: INA128, AD620, AD8221 (CMRR ≥ 100 dB)
Lab version: two followers + difference amp, all gain from R_{2}/R_{1}
slides.notes: The input stage improves the CMRR by the factor 1 + 2R/R_G. The lab circuit uses gain one in the buffers, so matching of R1 to R4 alone sets the CMRR.

slides.title: Finite gain and bandwidth
bullets: Split the gain: 10·100 → −0.11 %; rule of the lab: G < 100 per stage
Bandwidth f_{c} ≈ GBW/G: 1 MHz/100 = 10 kHz
Falstad has constant A = 10^{5}: no GBW, no slew rate
slides.rule: G_{real} = G/(1 + G/A);  GBW = A(f)·f = G·f_{c}

falstad.name: opamp_finite_gain
falstad.hint: One stage 0.990 V / 9.09 V vs. two stages 0.999 V / 9.98 V

slides.notes: At 1 kHz a 1 MHz op-amp has only A = 1000, so a G = 100 stage is 10 % low; check fast circuits against the data sheet. The capstone signal is a few hertz, so GBW is no problem there. Exercise 6.4.

slides.title: Output swing and single supply
bullets: Classic op-amp stays 1 … 2 V from the rails (LM358 at 5 V: 0 … 3.5 V)
Rail-to-rail output: within 10 mV … a few 100 mV of the rails
Check input common-mode range too: capstone bridge sits at 0.1 V
Single supply: bias bipolar signals to V_{S}/2, ±2 V → 0.5 … 4.5 V
Clipping cannot be repaired later: leave headroom for interference

falstad.name: opamp_level_shift
falstad.hint: Shifted output 0.5 … 4.5 V vs. the follower clipping below 0 V

slides.notes: Exactly 0 V output is impossible on a single 5 V supply: use a negative rail or an offset range like 0.1 to 4.1 V. A clipped 50 Hz interference turns into a DC error after the low-pass filter.

slides.title: Offset voltage and bias current
bullets: LM358: V_{OS} ≈ 2 mV, I_{B} ≈ 20 nA; CMOS: ≈ 1 mV, ≈ 1 pA
Zero-drift (OPA2333, MCP6V02): V_{OS} < 10 µV
Capstone: 2 mV × 107.6 = 0.22 V, 5 % of full scale, almost ½ LSB
Remedies: zero-drift or CMOS op-amp, low R_{S}, offset trimming

falstad.name: opamp_offset
falstad.hint: G = 101: 1 mV offset → 0.101 V; 100 nA via 100 kΩ → −1.01 V

slides.notes: Falstad's op-amp has no offset or bias current; the example models them with an extra voltage and current source. With the 100 Ω bridge source resistance I_B matters little, but behind a hold capacitor it does. Exercise 6.5.

slides.title: Capstone signal chain
bullets: Pt100 bridge at 4.00 V: V_{BR} = 0 … 37.18 mV
Stage 1: buffers + difference amp 100k/10k; stage 2: G_{2} = 10.76
Zero set by the bridge (R_{4} = 100 Ω), span by R_{F} in stage 2
Common mode only 0.1 V: op-amp inputs must work near the low rail
slides.notes: The following low-pass, S&H and 3-bit flash ADC expect exactly 0 to 4 V, so one LSB is 0.5 V. In hardware R_F is 91 kΩ plus a 10 kΩ trimmer (G2 = 10.1 to 11.1); Falstad uses the E96 value 97.6 kΩ or the trimmer at 6.6 kΩ.

slides.title: Design recipe: zero and span
steps: Bridge span V_{BR,max} and total gain G = V_{FS}/V_{BR,max} (107.6)
Split: G_{1} = 10 (buffers + diff. amp), G_{2} = G/G_{1} = 10.76
R_{F} = fixed part + trimmer: 91 kΩ + 10 kΩ
Zero: sensor at 100 Ω, check 0.00 V; correct via R_{4} or V_{REF}
Span: sensor at 138.5 Ω, trim to 4.00 V; then check the zero again
slides.notes: Zero first, then span: the span trimmer scales any remaining offset. The REF pin must be driven from a low impedance, as in the figure, or it spoils R4 and the CMRR.

slides.title: Falstad: the complete front end

falstad.name: opamp_ina
falstad.hint: Pt100 at 100 Ω → 0.00 V; at 138.5 Ω → V_diff 372 mV, Vout 4.00 V

observe: 50 Hz, 5 mV in series: 0.52 V at the output, no CMRR helps
Output needs headroom: 4 V + 0.52 V peak; low-pass must remove it
slides.notes: This is Exercise 6.6, the capstone amplifier. The 50 Hz interference is differential, so only the filter of the next chapter can remove it, below LSB/2 = 0.25 V.
